question: to the Commission Asger Christensen (Renew) Subject:

Soy is a crucial resource in animal feed production and therefore a key component of European livestock production. However, for the third year in a row, stakeholders in the EU soy value chain have signalled that they have been unable to source sufficient soy products. This is because the European Union Deforestation Regulation1 (EUDR) is entering into force imminently, and exporters of soy to the EU have been withholding their offers due to underlying legal uncertainty. If this situation persists, EU livestock farmers might not have enough feed for their animals. 1.

Is the Commission aware of the market disruption experienced by EU soy importers because of the EUDR, and what will the Commission do to ensure that after 30 December 2026 purchases of soybean products for animal feed use are not unduly blocked because of the EUDR?
What concrete measures will the Commission take to provide exporters and importers with sufficient legal certainty to ensure that soybean products continue to be offered and traded on the EU market?

If the EUDR risks restricting access to essential feed ingredients in practice, how will the Commission ensure that European livestock farmers do not end up paying the price for the legal uncertainty surrounding the regulation?

Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 (OJ L 150, 9.6.2023, p.206, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1115/oj). 1
